questions.question: In a classroom activity, students pick up green and white cocktail sticks from green grass in a limited time. What does this simple model demonstrate?
options: How plants absorb nutrients from the soil
Natural selection and the effect of camouflage
How seeds are dispersed by wind currents
The process of fossilisation over millions of years

questions.question: If we use green and white cocktail sticks on green grass to model natural selection, how would the prediction change if the grass became covered in white frost?
options: White sticks would become harder to see and survive better
Green sticks would become completely invisible
Both colours of sticks would be picked up at the exact same rate
No sticks would be picked up because the model stops working

questions.question: What is the scientific term for the special features that make an organism well suited to survive in its environment?
options: Acquired habits
Adaptations
Environmental factors
Generations

questions.question: How does having thick, white fur provide an advantage to a polar bear in its snowy environment?
options: It helps the bear absorb more sunlight to stay cool
It makes the bear run faster over the ice
It helps the bear blend into the snow to sneak up on prey
It allows the bear to swim without using its legs

questions.question: Why must individual organisms within a habitat compete with each other?
options: Because they want to help other species survive
Because resources like food and water are limited
Because they have identical genetic information
Because habitats have unlimited space for all living things

questions.question: Which of the following is a resource that plants specifically compete for in a crowded woodland?
options: Mates
Prey
Light
Oxygen for photosynthesis

questions.question: What is the main reason why some individual animals are able to compete more successfully for food than others of the same species?
options: They choose to change their features whenever they want
They have variations that make them better adapted to their environment
They do not need any energy to survive
They belong to a species that has never evolved

questions.question: What can natural selection cause to happen to the common characteristics of a species over many generations?
options: The characteristics remain completely identical forever
The characteristics can change, causing the species to evolve
The characteristics will change within each individual's own lifetime
The characteristics will become less suited to the environment

questions.question: In science, what is a "theory", such as the theory of evolution?
options: An educated guess made without any supporting evidence
A general explanation, developed from evidence, that explains many different examples
A set of rules that cannot be changed even if new evidence is found
A description of a single event that only happened once

questions.question: How do new advantageous features first appear in a population of organisms?
options: They are carefully planned in advance by the species
They appear randomly and are then maintained by natural selection
They are created by the organisms practicing new skills
They are passed down from other species that lived in different habitats

questions.question: An athlete trains hard and develops very large muscles during their lifetime. Why is this change not considered to be biological evolution?
options: Because it is a change in the features of an individual within its lifetime
Because large muscles are never useful for survival
Because the change was caused by a random genetic mutation
Because it happened over many generations of the athlete's family

questions.question: What are all fossils made of?
options: The original, undecomposed soft tissues of ancient animals
Mineralised remains of once-living organisms or traces left by them
Preserved plastic and metal materials from ancient civilisations
Hardened tree sap that contains no trace of living things

questions.question: What do fossils of dinosaurs, such as Triceratops, show us about these species today?
options: They are still living in remote parts of the world
They have gone extinct
They never actually existed
They evolved from modern-day birds within the last century

questions.question: Why must scientists be careful when making conclusions and explanations based on fossil evidence?
options: Fossils cannot be tested or examined with modern instruments
There are limitations to the conclusions and explanations that can be made from fossil evidence
Fossils only contain information about plants, never animals
All fossils are completely identical to organisms alive today

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of variation caused entirely by the environment or lifestyle?
options: Having blue eye colour
Having a scar from an injury
Having naturally curly hair
Having a biological blood group

questions.question: Why is environmental variation, such as a pierced ear or a suntan, not passed on to an organism's offspring?
options: Because it is not stored in the genetic information
Because offspring always look completely different from their parents
Because environmental variation is too dangerous for offspring
Because offspring only inherit features from their grandparents

questions.question: Why can genetic variation, such as the instructions for having camouflaged skin, be passed on to offspring?
options: Because it is caused by the lifestyle of the parents
Because it is heritable and stored in genetic information
Because offspring choose which genes they want to receive
Because it changes completely every time an animal reproduces

questions.question: According to the theory of natural selection, what is true about the "fittest" (better adapted) individuals in a population?
options: They are the ones that run the fastest in circles
They are more likely to survive and reproduce
They always have a shorter lifespan than poorly adapted individuals
They stop competing with other species for resources

questions.question: How can human activities, such as causing pollution or clearing forests, affect natural selection in a wild population?
options: They stop all variation from happening in the population
They can change the environmental conditions, which affects which individuals survive
They guarantee that every single organism will survive and reproduce
They prevent any genetic information from being passed to offspring

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, approximately how long ago did the first living organisms (microorganisms) appear on Earth?
options: Around 4.5 billion years ago
Around 3.8 billion years ago
Around 500 million years ago
Around 10 thousand years ago
